accelerators.note: Block-diffusion: drafts 16 tokens in parallel, target verifies in one pass. Lossless for greedy decoding.

hardware.notes: Fits on M4 Max 64GB for short context. OOM at 32K on 64GB due to DFlash hidden-state allocation (~68GB). 512GB safe for all context lengths.

known_issues: OOM at 32K context on 64GB — DFlash hidden-state buffer allocation (~68GB). Use 512GB nodes for long context.
Draft model z-lab/gemma-4-31B-it-DFlash must match target architecture exactly. Do not mix 31B draft with 26B-A4B target.
bstnxbt/dflash-mlx added Gemma 4 support on 2026-05-06 — use latest main branch.
Block size 16 is optimal. Larger blocks don't improve acceptance rate and waste compute on rejections.
MTP (Gemma 4 native 3x) and DFlash (6x) are complementary in principle but not yet tested together on MLX.

verified_on.notes: 42.3 tok/s at 912-token prompt (vs ~11 baseline). OOM at 32K context on 64GB.

hardware.notes: 17GB / 4 = ~4.3GB per shard. Absurd headroom on every node. Pure decode bandwidth play — 4 memory controllers in parallel.

known_issues: 4.3GB/shard is tiny — JACCL overhead may outweigh bandwidth gains for simple requests.
DFlash + JACCL combo untested on 27B. Test separately first.
Using Qwen3.5-27B until Qwen3.6-27B MLX quant is verified on JACCL.

artifact.architecture: MoE + DeltaNet hybrid (10 attn + 30 linear) + native MTP heads

params.note: Always-on in mlx-vlm v0.5.0+; no flag required.

accelerators.note: Native continuous batching via mlx-vlm v0.5.0 server; avoids the request-queue serialization problem of mlx_lm.server.
Wiki measurement: TQ+DFlash is the only config that survives past 49K context on node-N (Apr 2026 audit).

params.note_disabled: Off by default until Qwen 3.6-A3B-specific drafter is verified; the 3.5 drafter may work but adds risk.

accelerators.repo: https://github.com/bstnxbt/dflash-mlx (port reference); native in mlx-vlm v0.5.0
accelerators.note: Toggle to enabled=true once draft model is downloaded + verified. See dflash-turboquant-mlx wiki entry.

hardware.notes: mlx-vlm v0.5.0 added native continuous batching as default scheduler. Aggregate throughput at 4-16 concurrent should match per-trial single-stream within ~20%, vs mlx_lm.server which serializes (per 2026-05-08 measurement: 13-17 tok/s/trial at 4 concurrent).

known_issues: DFlash drafter for Qwen 3.6-A3B not yet downloaded — accelerator gated to enabled=false
mlx-vlm primary use case is Vision-Language Models; text-only Qwen 3.6 path is supported but less battle-tested than mlx_lm.server
Continuous batching has no explicit flag — verify via concurrent-load smoke test before declaring it active
asmi MlxVlm engine path uses uvicorn wrapper (per src/serve.rs comment about reload=True bugs); cold start is 2-4 min vs 1-2 min for mlx_lm.server

verified_on.notes: Profile created after 2026-05-08 dry-run post-mortem revealed mlx_lm.server lacks true continuous batching (4 concurrent trials measured 13-17 tok/s each vs ~140 tok/s expected solo). mlx-vlm v0.5.0 verified installed; first node-N serve + Harbor smoke test pending.

description: Qwen 3.6-35B-A3B served via mlx-vlm v0.5.0 — native continuous batching + TurboQuant 3.5-bit KV + DFlash speculative decoding (gated). The 'real' production profile: stacks three of the four wiki-tracked accelerators (DFlash/TurboQuant/continuous-batching) in one binary, no external drafter download for MTP path on supported models. Designed for `harbor run --n-concurrent 4` workloads where mlx_lm.server's request queue serializes (see 2026-05-08 dry-run post-mortem).

sampling.note: Use server-level `--enable-thinking` flag (off by default in v0.5.0) for the cleanest config; this extra_body is the per-request fallback if the server flag isn't set.

known_issues: mlx_vlm server has NO concurrency flag — concurrency is server-side request handling, not a launch arg. --help exposes only draft/kv/thinking/vision options.
asmi /serve/stop takes ?port=N as a QUERY PARAM. A JSON body {"port":N} is ignored and it stops the wrong server (this took down an unrelated Holo-3.1 server).
asmi's watchdog respawns managed serve slots, so `kill` on a managed pid is futile — it returns within seconds.
